questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to a country where the spoken languages was English, and a place where I could live on campus.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Upon arrival I had plenty of dialog with the the Study Abroad office at NCS, which made my arrival perfect.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They greeted me and drove me to my accommodation. The day after there was a ice-cream day, where you could say "hello" to the fellow exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There very plenty of options both on and off campus. Off campus required more information and in my opinion only suitable for bigger groups. Lets say you were 3-4 from the same University studying abroad together. On campus accommodation application was easy and done through the University webpage where there was pictures of the different apartments.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There were 3-4 meal plans. I choose to cook for myself, since I choose a apartment with a kitchen

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There is some apartments where there is only a microwave. In that case you should definitely get a meal plane. Otherwise I thought it was fun to buy groceries because the products was different than the regular products you see in Europe.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You apply with your grades. The grades is the decider on wether you get a spot or not. After you receive a spot there is some work to do with the application process, but UCPH have a intuitive formula you use.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You get a study abroad coordinator you can write to if you are in doubt about anything. Other than that there will be a meeting I would recommend to attend where most of the stuff about pre arrival is explained.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I didn't get all my classes I applied for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend to apply for credits to multiply courses (more than you want to take) at your home University
so there is something you can choose between in case of you don't get the classes you want. (I didn't do it and got sorted it out anyway, but it is good to have applied for more classes than you intend to take.)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was easier than expected. The amount of math was unveiling compared to UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style was more interactive oral discussion with the students and professor.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Marketing Methods
International Financial Management
Money, Financial Markets, and the Economy
Introduction to Resource and Environmental Economics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the course International Financial Management which build upon financial decision making but with a more international approach, and the professor was really fun and good.

questions.answer:
- I had to apply and pay for Canadian visum even though I only had lay-over in Toronto for 2 hours. 
- Sheets
- Blanket

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries was more expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did spent the most of my time playing golf.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was plenty of clubs available. From football, Rugby, Soccer, Golf, Disc Golf, Bee-club, Computer gaming etc...

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to excess the opportunity to play sports you don't play as much in Europe. (Wall-climbing, Pickelball, Basketball, American Football)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Rent a car and see the country-side. Outer banks is also magnificent. 
I did spent my Spring Break in Miami which was early cheap to fly to, but also an expensive city to life in.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy. People are so welcome and out-spoken in the US.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Go to local bar - Mitches Tavern. 
Sign up for sports or other clubs of your interest. 
Speak with your classmates. They will probably try to speak with you :)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The open-minded and welcoming attitude I liked a lot. Every time you got off the bus at night the bus driver yelled "Please, stay safe my son".

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Sheets 
Money 
Money

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get pay-pall and watch app installed before hand.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding thing was the friendships I got and the experience of have discussion about the subjects with the professor.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Missing my friends and family.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
